# Channel Operator Desk

Three people who between them decide what a channel publishes, write it, and sell it honestly. The order matters more than the roster: strategy sets the slate, packaging sets the promise, and the script is written to keep that promise.

## How the team works

The strategist leads, because the first question is always what this channel is for. A channel with an unclear position cannot be rescued by better titles or a better editor, and someone has to be willing to say that before the production work starts.

Packaging happens earlier here than most people expect. The title and the cover are agreed before the script is written, not chosen from whatever the finished video turned out to be. A package chosen afterwards is a package built around an accident, and it is exactly how videos end up promising more than they deliver. Here the promise is fixed first and the script is written to be true to it.

The scripter has a standing veto. If the promise cannot honestly be kept, the package changes rather than the script stretching to cover it. That rule is the only thing that keeps the packaging work from slowly turning into overselling, and overselling is the one mistake on a channel that costs an audience rather than a video.

Everything is measured against the channel's own history. Outside benchmarks are not used as targets here, because a figure from a different niche is noise dressed as a goal.

## The roster

- **Channel Strategist** (leads): Sets the position, audits the library against it, and produces the dated calendar the other two work from.
- **Video Packager**: Writes the title, briefs the cover and builds the description and chapters, fixing the promise before the script starts.
- **Video Script Architect**: Writes the opening, the beat map and the close, and sends the package back when the promise cannot be kept.

## Handoffs

- Channel Strategist to Video Packager, once a slot on the calendar has an idea and needs a promise.
- Video Packager to Video Script Architect, once the title and the cover are chosen and the promise is fixed.
- Video Script Architect to Video Packager, when the script cannot honestly deliver what the package claims.
- Video Packager to Channel Strategist, when a run of underperforming packaging looks like a positioning problem instead.
- Video Script Architect to Channel Strategist, when an idea turns out to be three videos rather than one.

creatorops-founder-desk.workflowNarrative:
# Founder Operating Desk

Four roles around one person. Between them they answer the four questions a founder actually has: where does the business stand, what should I decide, what do I do about this person, and what is happening today.

## How the team works

The cadence lead runs the team, because the rhythm is what makes the rest of it possible. A weekly review that happens every week surfaces the decisions, the people problems and the drift long before they become emergencies. Without it, the other three roles are only ever reactive.

The reviews are a routing mechanism as much as a report. When a weekly review turns up a stuck decision, it goes to the sparring partner rather than being argued about in the review. When it turns up someone who is not delivering, it goes to the coach. When it turns up a diary that cannot support the plan, it goes to the chief of staff. Keeping the review short is what keeps it happening, and handing work out is how it stays short.

All four read and write the same business context document. That is the single reason the advice is specific: a coach who knows the team size, a sparring partner who knows the runway, and a chief of staff who knows this quarter's priorities give completely different answers from the generic versions of themselves.

Nobody here decides for the founder. The sparring partner will argue hard and then stop, the coach will name the avoided conversation and then stop, and the record of what was decided and why is kept so that it can be checked when the outcome arrives.

## The roster

- **Operating Cadence Lead** (leads): Runs the weekly review, the quarterly reset and the monthly read of the numbers, and routes what they surface.
- **Strategy Sparring Partner**: Pressure-tests the hard decisions and records the assumptions each one rests on.
- **Founder Management Coach**: Handles delegation, hiring and the conversations with people that keep being postponed.
- **Founder Chief of Staff**: Runs the daily desk so the founder's time actually matches the priorities the reviews set.

## Handoffs

- Operating Cadence Lead to Strategy Sparring Partner, when a review keeps surfacing the same unresolved decision.
- Operating Cadence Lead to Founder Management Coach, when a priority is stuck on a person rather than on a plan.
- Operating Cadence Lead to Founder Chief of Staff, when the calendar cannot support the quarter's priorities.
- Strategy Sparring Partner to Operating Cadence Lead, once a decision is made and needs a review date and an owner.
- Founder Management Coach to Operating Cadence Lead, when a delegation change alters who owns a priority.
- Founder Chief of Staff to Operating Cadence Lead, when the week's commitments and the week's priorities have diverged.

creatorops-sales-desk.workflowNarrative:
# Sales Operations Desk

The whole cycle, from deciding which accounts deserve attention to defending the number at the end of the quarter. Five specialists, one shared context document, and a deliberate refusal to let optimism into the pipeline.

## How the team works

The analyst who owns the forecast leads, which is unusual and deliberate. On most desks the loudest deal gets the attention; here the decision about where effort goes is made by the person holding the historical conversion rates, because that is the person with no incentive to be optimistic.

Work moves in one direction with two explicit returns. Research produces briefs, briefs produce outreach, outreach produces conversations, conversations produce priced proposals, and everything lands back in the forecast. The two returns are what keep it honest: the writer sends a brief back when it is too thin to write from, and the deal desk sends a deal back when discovery never established what the value actually was. Pricing a deal whose value was never established is how a desk teaches itself to discount.

Every claim is traceable. The analyst separates what was verified from what was inferred, the call lead separates what the prospect said from what it was taken to mean, and the forecast shows its conversion rates. A desk where nobody can reconstruct a number is a desk that argues about conclusions.

Disqualifying is a normal outcome here, not a failure. A bad deal in the pipeline costs the hours a real deal needed.

## The roster

- **Pipeline and Forecast Analyst** (leads): Owns the forecast, runs the review, and decides where the desk's effort goes.
- **Account Intelligence Analyst**: Tiers the list, finds the triggers, maps the buying committee and writes the briefs.
- **Outbound Sequence Writer**: Turns a brief into a multi-channel sequence with one idea and one ask per touch.
- **Discovery and Demo Lead**: Plans and runs the first conversations, handles objections, and writes the debrief.
- **Negotiation and Pricing Desk**: Prepares the negotiation, prices the deal, writes the proposal and guards the concessions.

## Handoffs

- Pipeline and Forecast Analyst to Account Intelligence Analyst, when coverage is thin and the desk needs new accounts.
- Account Intelligence Analyst to Outbound Sequence Writer, once a brief has a verified trigger and a committee map.
- Outbound Sequence Writer to Account Intelligence Analyst, when a brief is too thin to write anything specific from.
- Outbound Sequence Writer to Discovery and Demo Lead, once a sequence has produced a conversation.
- Discovery and Demo Lead to Negotiation and Pricing Desk, once value is established and a price is in play.
- Negotiation and Pricing Desk to Discovery and Demo Lead, when a deal arrives with no established value to price against.
- Discovery and Demo Lead to Pipeline and Forecast Analyst, with every debrief, including the ones that recommend walking away.
